subject: Conveyor enablement: onboarding itinerary, schema freeze & runtime checklist
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@wellpath.ai>; Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@wellpath.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conveyor enablement kickoff: itinerary, schema freeze & runtime checklist

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Great to meet you virtually this week. Following our demo, I wanted to share a pragmatic onboarding itinerary for the "Conveyor" feature set (streaming + tool calling + structured JSON outputs). Goal: get a production canary running in your staging environment and freeze the output schema for the v1-release.

High-level timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): mutual action plan + SOW signoff — see attached WP_SOW_v3.pdf
- Week 1: schema alignment workshop (we'll iterate on streaming-schema-draft.json)
- Week 2: runtime integration + tooling (function/tool calling wiring, batching & KV cache settings)
- Week 3: canary rollout, tracing hooks, and observability checks
- Week 4: production cutover & post-launch monitoring runbook

Key asks from WellPath AI:
1) Confirm which API routes will call Conveyor (list 2–3 canonical endpoints).
2) Share one or two representative transcripts to help scope structured-output fields.
3) Confirm compliance/retention requirements (so we configure logs/trace retention appropriately).

Attachments included: streaming-schema-draft.json (working draft), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (editable plan).

Technical notes for your engineering team:
- For streaming we recommend a 1s partial-flush cadence and prefix caching for repeat user prompts to reduce token cost.
- Tool/function calls: we'll supply a lightweight shim to validate signatures; prefer JSON-RPC style handler for the first pass.
- Structured outputs: we want to freeze the high-level object shape by the end of Week 1 to avoid downstream schema drift during the canary.

Next step: can you confirm availability for a 60-minute schema workshop next Tuesday (Aug 3)? If that works we’ll send a calendar invite with pre-read.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0183

From: Alicia Barnes <alicia@wellpath.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@wellpath.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conveyor enablement kickoff: itinerary, schema freeze & runtime checklist

Thanks Soojin — this looks reasonable.

Tom and I reviewed the SOW and the proposed cadence. We can commit to the Week 1 workshop and have engineering resources for Week 2. A few quick clarifications:

- API surface: primary endpoints are /v1/assist and /v1/triage — both will need streaming in the first phase.
- Transcripts: I'll upload two anonymized transcripts to the Drive link you provided by Monday.
- Data retention: we retain traces for 90 days; customer PII is removed before anything leaves our environment. We'll send an evidence note for the SOC2 checklist.

Aug 3 at 10am PT works for the schema workshop. Please send the calendar invite.

Also, question from our infra lead: what runtime variant do you recommend for low-latency 99th-percentile (we're on GCP)?

Best,
Alicia
Head of Integrations, WellPath AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@wellpath.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@wellpath.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conveyor enablement kickoff: itinerary, schema freeze & runtime checklist

Alicia — quick note from runtime/infra side: for GCP we generally recommend a dedicated P4d-style instance family for the canary if you need 99th-percentile latency under 300ms for token streams. If cost is a concern, we can provision a mixed-pool approach (smaller quantized variants for lower-cost fallback + a high-perf variant for low-latency paths).

Implementation checklist I'm proposing for Week 2 (brief):
- Auth + routing: service account permissions and firewall rules for private-link (if you want VPC peering).
- Streaming: client-side chunk aggregation + server-side partial-flush at 1s intervals.
- Tool calls: validate JSON schema at ingress and attach a request-id header for tracing.
- Observability: wire tracing hooks to the Redwood Console (token-level timing and error-tagging).

I'll bring a short ops-setup checklist to the workshop and we can walk through a sample call.

—Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Conveyor enablement kickoff: itinerary, schema freeze & runtime checklist

Thanks everyone — appreciate the clarity. Quick operational notes after our infra sync this afternoon: 

- We can run the canary on a single high-perf instance (P4-style) in us-west1 and route 10% of traffic there initially.
- We've uploaded two scrubbed transcripts to the Drive link: drive.google.com/file/d/abc123 (shared with soojin and karthik).
- SOC evidence: sending the retention note to Monica shortly.

Two asks for Redwood before the workshop:
1) A short pre-read (1 pager) that shows how function/tool calling event flow maps to our webhook handlers.
2) A minimal validation JSON for the structured output (example payload + schema snippet) so our frontend can wire the acceptance tests.

If you can drop the pre-read and a minimal schema snippet into the Drive folder before Tuesday we'll be ready to run the workshop with eng leads.

Tom
VP Product Engineering, WellPath AI
notes: Thread recorded in Soojin's inbox; attachments are referenced but stored in Drive.
